# Metering data consumption contract for chargeback reporting

## Description

Resolves the strategy's open question: the metering data schema is owned by the
in-flight RHAISTRAT-9990 strategy (GPU usage metering) and is not final until
that strategy lands, yet the chargeback reporting built here consumes it. This
investigation determines how the reporting work should consume that in-flight
data — producing a documented consumption contract and a decision on how to
proceed given the external timing risk — so the reporting implementation starts
against a stable, testable interface instead of either waiting blind or
hard-coupling to a moving schema. It does not design or implement any part of
the metering collection pipeline (owned by RHAISTRAT-9990).

## Scope

- Inventory the current draft metering data schema as delivered by
  RHAISTRAT-9990: fields, per-project GPU-hour semantics, granularity, and data
  availability/retention assumptions relevant to reporting.
- Assess schema stability: which parts are settled, which changes are
  anticipated before RHAISTRAT-9990 finalizes, and what coordination with the
  metering strategy's team is needed.
- Decide the consumption approach for the chargeback reporting backend:
  consume the draft schema directly with fixture-backed contract tests,
  introduce an isolating adaptation layer between the metering data and report
  computation, or defer consuming work until the schema finalizes.
- Define precise acceptance criteria that mark "metering data available /
  schema final" (RHAISTRAT-9990 landed) for unblocking final validation of the
  reporting work.
- Document the recommended path, the trade-offs, and the bounded outcome space
  so downstream planning can proceed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The draft metering data schema (fields, per-project GPU-hour semantics,
  granularity) is documented, with open or anticipated changes explicitly
  listed.
- A consumption approach decision is recorded — direct consumption with
  contract fixtures, an isolating adaptation layer, or deferral — with the
  trade-offs that justify it.
- The criteria that mark the metering data as final and available
  (RHAISTRAT-9990 landed) are defined precisely enough to serve as acceptance
  criteria for downstream reporting validation.
- If the recommended approach is to build before the schema finalizes, the
  contract fixtures and test strategy that isolate reporting from schema churn
  are specified.

## HLR Traceability

- Enables HLR-1 and HLR-2 by resolving the strategy's open question on
  consuming the in-flight metering data schema (Open Questions #1). No HLR is
  directly implemented by this epic.

# Chargeback reporting backend: per-project GPU-hour reports, stable API, and CSV export

## Description

Delivers the server side of chargeback reporting: computation of per-project
GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges from the metering data
delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990, exposed through a stable API for finance tooling
and as CSV exports. Reports are in GPU-hours — no currency or cost-rate
modelling — and this epic consumes metering data only; it does not re-implement
metering collection, which is owned by RHAISTRAT-9990.

## Scope

- Report computation: aggregate per-project GPU-hour consumption over
  selectable time ranges from the metering data, following the consumption
  contract resolved by the metering-consumption investigation.
- A stable reporting API through which finance tooling can retrieve
  per-project consumption reports programmatically.
- CSV export of the reports.
- Binding of the report computation to the metering data source per the
  documented consumption contract: implementation may proceed against contract
  fixture data, with final end-to-end validation against real metering data
  once RHAISTRAT-9990 lands (external precondition, acceptance-gated).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given available metering data (or contract fixtures standing in for it during
  development), per-project GPU-hour consumption can be retrieved for a
  selectable time range via the reporting API, and the reported values match
  the underlying metering data.
- Reports can be exported as CSV, and the CSV content is consistent with the
  API-served report data.
- The reporting API surface (served endpoints and report fields) is
  documented, and the documented surface is covered by fixture-backed
  contract tests — any change to the served surface is reflected in the API
  documentation and caught by those tests, so finance-tooling integrations
  are not silently broken.
- When real metering data from RHAISTRAT-9990 is available, end-to-end report
  values match the metered per-project GPU-hours (final validation gate for
  this epic).
- No metering collection is implemented in this scope — consumption only; the
  metering pipeline remains owned by RHAISTRAT-9990.
- Reports are denominated in GPU-hours; no currency or cost-rate conversion is
  introduced.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time
  ranges — report computation and retrieval.
- HLR-2 (P1): CSV export and retrieval via a stable API for finance tooling.

# Per-project Kueue GPU quota exposure for consumption reporting

## Description

Delivers the Distributed Workloads side of the quota comparison: makes each
project's Kueue GPU quota available in a form the Dashboard admin reporting
view can consume, so that current-month GPU-hour consumption can be shown
against each project's quota. This work is independent of the metering data
delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990 and can proceed immediately.

## Scope

- Expose per-project Kueue GPU quota — per the platform's ClusterQueue /
  LocalQueue quota model — through a documented consumption contract (access
  surface and data shape) shared with the consuming Dashboard reporting work,
  including the mapping from projects to their applicable quotas.
- Validate that the exposed quota data matches the configured Kueue quotas.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-project GPU quota data is exposed for consumption by the Dashboard
  admin reporting view via the documented consumption contract (access
  surface and data shape), and the exposed data conforms to that contract.
- Exposed quota values match the configured Kueue quota configuration,
  spot-checked across projects with differing quotas.
- The mapping from projects to their applicable quotas is complete for projects
  participating in the platform's distributed workload queues.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): the Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption against
  each project's Kueue quota — the per-project quota data side.
